summary: This PR adds a new server-side proxy route (/api/module-chain) that byte-for-byte mirrors the existing, already-audited /api/capability-tree route (same requireAuth() gate, same org-scoped callVeridian() call, same error shape), so the VERIDIAN Bearer key stays server-side and the new module tree is correctly tenant-scoped -- no security regression. veri-chat-context.tsx merges the construction tree and the new module-chain tree in parallel via a fault-isolated fetchJsonNodes() helper (one source failing no longer breaks the other, an improvement over the prior unguarded fetch), and is covered by 4 new real unit tests. VeriComposer.tsx correctly gates dispatch (queueCurrent/send/button-disabled state) behind a new isDispatchableChain check tied to CONSTRUCTION_CHAIN_MODE_KEY = "construction_intelligence" -- verified this literal matches the real top-level key /api/capability-tree returns (confirmed via existing e2e/copilot-chat.spec.ts assertion), so existing construction dispatch functionality is preserved and the new GRC/ERP module chain is correctly restricted to browse-only until a real cross-module dispatch allowlist is built (a reasonable, explicitly documented scope cut, not a silent gap). The diff is purely additive (new route, new tests, extended context/composer logic), does not touch .github/workflows/**, auth/migrations/schema/*.sql/permission/payment/billing/rls/security paths, or env files, and the deletion count does not approach the tier2 heavy-deletion threshold, so the tier1 classification is correct.
